answer: Every identity pins one row on a public canyon table, staking an 80-credit bond. Each row holds a thread only its key can extend. A whisper audit replays threads each epoch; a copied row or one key on two rows burns both bonds. First row costs 55, the k-th 55+7(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 3,551,500 and lock 80,000 against a 40,000 pool. A rented row still names its lender's key; the lender burns too. Honest agents pay 55 once and keep their bond.
